To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

adsorption of metal ions onto the bacterial surface can influence the concentration of the metal ion at the bacterial surface and that the magnitude of the adsorbed metal ion is linearly proportional with the magnitude of the observed chemotactic response.

Ni2+ adsorbs onto the cell surface of E. coli and influences its chemotactic response, and that the concentration of Ni adsorbed onto the cell surface is linearly proportional with the magnitude of the repellent response.
the chemotactic responses of E. coli to Ni2+ are influenced by Ni2+ adsorbed onto its surface.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of adsorption on the chemotactic responses of bacteria to chemical effector molecules.
the influence of adsorption reactions on the ability of bacteria to sense chemical gradients in their environment.
understanding how the surface properties of bacteria influence the chemotaxis response.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the chemotactic behavior of bacteria in response to Ni2+, or other metal ions, is dependent on both the speciation of metal ions and the surface chemistry of the bacteria.
the adsorption of nickel ions to the cell surface is a significant factor in the response of E. coli to nickel.

the adsorption of Ni(2+) to the cell surface of E. coli influences the chemotactic responses of E. coli to Ni(2+) and that this effect can be quantified by a simple model that incorporates the protonation state and speciation of Ni(2+).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the adsorption of Ni on E. coli can influence its chemotactic response.
the concentration of an effector in solution is not the only important factor for chemotactic response.
the adsorption of Ni to E. coli cells is a key factor for chemotaxis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
chemotactic responses to chemical effectors are dependent on environmental conditions.
adsorption of metal species to bacterial surfaces is a significant factor in chemotaxis.
the speciation of a chemoattractant or chemorepellent and the protonation of the bacterial cell surface must be considered in the design and interpretation of chemotactic measurements.
